findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the utility sink was observed coming apart. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspector that a ticket will be put in for the caulking repairs on the utility sink. Ensure that the utility sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review with staff and ensure that hand washing is taking place correctly at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani bucket in the front area of the facility would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Shift change had just taken place and the buckets were in the process of being changed. Once changed the concentration was correct and the violation corrected. Education was conducted with the PIC and it was suggested that the buckets be changed more often to ensure that they do not fall below minimum concentration requirements at any time.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: The inspector observes at least 8 fruit flies and three house flies on the front line.  Inspector is waiting for proof of pest control to see that directions are being followed. The facility should have more than maintenance visits at this time due to the presence of pests. The facility has had a light trap for flying insects installed in the dry storage, and the brush guard replaced on the back receiving door. Keeping the drains and area under the line dry and clean is suggested. Clean all the way to the back of the wall floor juncture. Also make best effort to ensure that the display case is free of insects even thought the food in the case is not served to the public. 
July 14 - 16 the facility is going to have plumbing repairs done at the cold bar drain area. This should also help with the pest control issue. 
PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The facility has no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at the time of inspection. The facility must be under the supervision of a CFPM at all times. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed a gap in the back door at the right lower corner. Repair or replace the door seal as soon as possible to deter pests from entering the facility. 

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Fruit flies are observed in the pastry case and in various places around the facility, in the back stock and at the front line. The food in the pastry case is for show only and is not served. The facility is under contract with a pest control company who is scheduled out Thursday, 6/20 to do treatment. A follow up will be conducted on July 1, 2024. Follow PCO guidelines to eliminate pests. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed boxes of single use cups, lids and towels on the floor of the back-stock room. Take care to store single use articles properly to protect them from potential contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Seal on the tea side bar cooler is in disrepair. The seal is not functioning properly and does not allow the cooler to fully shut. Also it is no longer smooth or easily cleanable. Replace seal as soon as possible to help maintain cooler temperature.

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed milk coolers in back to be soiled in the bottom with dry crusty milk. Clean the coolers and maintain then clean on the inside and out. 
  
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the areas under upright freezers in the back-stock room to be littered. Also, floors through out the back were soiled. The condenser fan covers are also soiled with dust accumulation. Clean and maintain these areas clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arrival, the hand sink at the sandwich area was not provided with disposable towels. Facility states that towels are on the truck and should arrive in a couple of hours. The facility provided napkins to the sink for hand drying. The violation is considered corrected on site. Continue to provide single use hand drying supplies at the sinks until the towels arrive. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed sanitation buckets and trays used to sanitize the steam wands at 100ppm of quat sanitizer. The sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at 200ppm. Inspector suggests to pull sanitizer into buckets and wet clean dry wiping cloths with sanitizer from dispenser before adding them to the sanitation buckets. The buckets were pulled and replaced with sanitizer from the 3 part dispenser. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a box of pumps to be stored on the floor next to the ice machine. The box of pumps was moved back up onto the shelf where they are normally stored. Take care to store food and food contact items at least 6 inches up off of the floor. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed caulking at both customer bathroom hand sinks to be coming away from the wall and sink. Repair caulk by re-caulking these two hand sinks. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed food boxes and single-use food utensils stored on floor of back room. Boxes should be at least 6 inches above the floor. Discussed with PIC.
